title: Problem 1.1
context_text: $Q_d=\{0,1\}^d$ is the $d$-dimensional hypercube. $f(d)$ is the number of partitions (tilings) of the vertex set of $Q_d$ into classes each spanning a subcube (a set of vertices obtained by fixing some coordinates and letting the others vary), and for $S\subseteq\{0,1,\dots,d\}$, $f_S(d)$ counts those partitions in which every class has dimension in $S$; thus $f_{\le2}(d)$ counts partitions into singletons, edges and 2-dimensional subcubes, $f_2(d)$ partitions into 2-dimensional subcubes only, and $f_{0,r}(d)$ partitions into singletons and $r$-dimensional subcubes. $m(d)=f_1(d)$ and $m'(d)=f_{\le1}(d)$ are the numbers of perfect matchings and of all matchings of $Q_d$. Write $n=2^{d-1}$ (the size of each side of the bipartite graph $Q_d$) and $N=(d/e)^n$, a rough estimate of $m(d)$. The trivial hierarchy is $m(d)\le m'(d)\le f_{\le2}(d)\le f(d)$. Problem (i) is classical: Graham and Harary computed $m(1),\dots,m(5)=1,2,9,272,589185$, and Östergård and Pettersson computed $m(6)$ and $m(7)$; the first values of $f(d)$ from $d=0$ are $1,2,8,154,89512,71319425714$ (OEIS A018926). Problem (iii) was raised by Gadouleau at the 29th British Combinatorial Conference in 2022, and (iv) is introduced by the authors as a closely related variant. The authors prove $e^{n/2d}N\le m(d)\le 2^{(1+o(1))\log d\cdot n/(2d)}N$, $m'(d)=m(d)\,2^{\Theta(n/\sqrt d)}$ (so $m'(d)/m(d)$ is subexponential in $n$), $c^n m'(d)\le f_{\le2}(d)$ for some constant $c>1$ (so $f_{\le2}(d)/m'(d)$ and $f(d)/m(d)$ are at least exponential in $n$), $f(d)\le(d+1)^n\le e^{n+n/d}N$ (so $f(d)/m(d)$ is at most exponential), and for every fixed $r\ge2$, $N^{r/2^{r-1}-o(1)}\le f_{0,r}(d)\le f_{\{0\}\cup\{r,r+1,\dots\}}(d)\le N^{r/2^{r-1}+o(1)}$. These give the main term of $m(d)$ and partial answers to the other parts.
notes: Part (iii) attributed to Gadouleau (2022, unpublished talk); parts (i), (ii), (iv) are the authors' own formulations.
paper_title: Partitioning the hypercube into smaller hypercubes

title: Problem 1.2
statement_text:
What is the order of magnitude of the
following ratios? In particular, which one of them is an
exponential function of $n$? 
(i) $m^{\prime}(d)/m(d)$,   (ii) $f_{\leq 2}(d)/m^{\prime}(d)$,
  (iii) $f(d)/f_{\leq 2}(d),$    (iv) $f(d)/m(d)$.
context_text: $Q_d=\{0,1\}^d$ is the $d$-dimensional hypercube. $f(d)$ is the number of partitions (tilings) of the vertex set of $Q_d$ into classes each spanning a subcube (a set of vertices obtained by fixing some coordinates and letting the others vary), and for $S\subseteq\{0,1,\dots,d\}$, $f_S(d)$ counts those partitions in which every class has dimension in $S$; thus $f_{\le2}(d)$ counts partitions into singletons, edges and 2-dimensional subcubes, $f_2(d)$ partitions into 2-dimensional subcubes only, and $f_{0,r}(d)$ partitions into singletons and $r$-dimensional subcubes. $m(d)=f_1(d)$ and $m'(d)=f_{\le1}(d)$ are the numbers of perfect matchings and of all matchings of $Q_d$. Write $n=2^{d-1}$ (the size of each side of the bipartite graph $Q_d$) and $N=(d/e)^n$, a rough estimate of $m(d)$. The hierarchy $m(d)\le m'(d)\le f_{\le2}(d)\le f(d)$ holds by definition, and 'exponential function of $n$' refers to $n=2^{d-1}$. The authors prove $e^{n/2d}N\le m(d)\le 2^{(1+o(1))\log d\cdot n/(2d)}N$, $m'(d)=m(d)\,2^{\Theta(n/\sqrt d)}$ (so $m'(d)/m(d)$ is subexponential in $n$), $c^n m'(d)\le f_{\le2}(d)$ for some constant $c>1$ (so $f_{\le2}(d)/m'(d)$ and $f(d)/m(d)$ are at least exponential in $n$), $f(d)\le(d+1)^n\le e^{n+n/d}N$ (so $f(d)/m(d)$ is at most exponential), and for every fixed $r\ge2$, $N^{r/2^{r-1}-o(1)}\le f_{0,r}(d)\le f_{\{0\}\cup\{r,r+1,\dots\}}(d)\le N^{r/2^{r-1}+o(1)}$. Hence the paper answers (i) (subexponential), (ii) (at least exponential) and (iv) (exponential in $n$); part (iii), whether $f(d)/f_{\le2}(d)$ is subexponential, remains open and is asked separately by the authors.

title: Problem 1.9
statement_text: Determine the asymptotic behaviour of the number $f_{2}(d).$
context_text: $Q_d=\{0,1\}^d$ is the $d$-dimensional hypercube. $f(d)$ is the number of partitions (tilings) of the vertex set of $Q_d$ into classes each spanning a subcube (a set of vertices obtained by fixing some coordinates and letting the others vary), and for $S\subseteq\{0,1,\dots,d\}$, $f_S(d)$ counts those partitions in which every class has dimension in $S$; thus $f_{\le2}(d)$ counts partitions into singletons, edges and 2-dimensional subcubes, $f_2(d)$ partitions into 2-dimensional subcubes only, and $f_{0,r}(d)$ partitions into singletons and $r$-dimensional subcubes. $m(d)=f_1(d)$ and $m'(d)=f_{\le1}(d)$ are the numbers of perfect matchings and of all matchings of $Q_d$. Write $n=2^{d-1}$ (the size of each side of the bipartite graph $Q_d$) and $N=(d/e)^n$, a rough estimate of $m(d)$. The authors prove that for every fixed $r\ge2$, $N^{r/2^{r-1}-o(1)}\le f_{0,r}(d)\le N^{r/2^{r-1}+o(1)}$, which for $r=2$ gives $f_{0,2}(d)=N^{1+o(1)}$; since $f_2(d)\le f_{0,2}(d)$, the upper bound $f_2(d)\le N^{1+o(1)}$ holds. It is natural to ask what happens when only 2-dimensional subcubes are allowed, and the authors believe that the same bound holds, i.e. $f_2(d)=N^{1+o(1)}$, but the lower bound is not proved.

title: Informal conjecture on $f_2(d)$
statement_text: The number $f_2(d)$ of partitions of the vertex set of $Q_d$ into 2-dimensional subcubes satisfies the same bound as $f_{0,2}(d)$, namely $N^{1-o(1)}\le f_2(d)\le N^{1+o(1)}$, where $N=(d/e)^{2^{d-1}}$.
context_text: $Q_d=\{0,1\}^d$ is the $d$-dimensional hypercube. $f(d)$ is the number of partitions (tilings) of the vertex set of $Q_d$ into classes each spanning a subcube (a set of vertices obtained by fixing some coordinates and letting the others vary), and for $S\subseteq\{0,1,\dots,d\}$, $f_S(d)$ counts those partitions in which every class has dimension in $S$; thus $f_{\le2}(d)$ counts partitions into singletons, edges and 2-dimensional subcubes, $f_2(d)$ partitions into 2-dimensional subcubes only, and $f_{0,r}(d)$ partitions into singletons and $r$-dimensional subcubes. $m(d)=f_1(d)$ and $m'(d)=f_{\le1}(d)$ are the numbers of perfect matchings and of all matchings of $Q_d$. Write $n=2^{d-1}$ (the size of each side of the bipartite graph $Q_d$) and $N=(d/e)^n$, a rough estimate of $m(d)$. The authors prove that for every fixed $r\ge2$, $N^{r/2^{r-1}-o(1)}\le f_{0,r}(d)\le N^{r/2^{r-1}+o(1)}$, i.e. $f_{0,2}(d)=N^{1\pm o(1)}$ for $r=2$; since $f_2(d)\le f_{0,2}(d)$ the upper bound transfers, and the belief is that the lower bound $N^{1-o(1)}$ also holds for partitions into 2-dimensional subcubes only. This belief motivates their problem of determining the asymptotic behaviour of $f_2(d)$.
notes: Stated in prose without a labelled environment, directly preceding Problem 1.9.

title: Problem 1.10
statement_text:
Is it true that
$f(d)/f_{\leq 2}(d)$ is subexponential in $n$?
context_text: $Q_d=\{0,1\}^d$ is the $d$-dimensional hypercube. $f(d)$ is the number of partitions (tilings) of the vertex set of $Q_d$ into classes each spanning a subcube (a set of vertices obtained by fixing some coordinates and letting the others vary), and for $S\subseteq\{0,1,\dots,d\}$, $f_S(d)$ counts those partitions in which every class has dimension in $S$; thus $f_{\le2}(d)$ counts partitions into singletons, edges and 2-dimensional subcubes, $f_2(d)$ partitions into 2-dimensional subcubes only, and $f_{0,r}(d)$ partitions into singletons and $r$-dimensional subcubes. $m(d)=f_1(d)$ and $m'(d)=f_{\le1}(d)$ are the numbers of perfect matchings and of all matchings of $Q_d$. Write $n=2^{d-1}$ (the size of each side of the bipartite graph $Q_d$) and $N=(d/e)^n$, a rough estimate of $m(d)$. The hierarchy $m(d)\le m'(d)\le f_{\le2}(d)\le f(d)$ holds by definition, and the authors ask which of the ratios is exponential in $n$. The authors prove $e^{n/2d}N\le m(d)\le 2^{(1+o(1))\log d\cdot n/(2d)}N$, $m'(d)=m(d)\,2^{\Theta(n/\sqrt d)}$ (so $m'(d)/m(d)$ is subexponential in $n$), $c^n m'(d)\le f_{\le2}(d)$ for some constant $c>1$ (so $f_{\le2}(d)/m'(d)$ and $f(d)/m(d)$ are at least exponential in $n$), $f(d)\le(d+1)^n\le e^{n+n/d}N$ (so $f(d)/m(d)$ is at most exponential), and for every fixed $r\ge2$, $N^{r/2^{r-1}-o(1)}\le f_{0,r}(d)\le f_{\{0\}\cup\{r,r+1,\dots\}}(d)\le N^{r/2^{r-1}+o(1)}$. So the remaining case is the ratio $f(d)/f_{\le2}(d)$. Evidence that small subcubes matter: the authors show $f_{\{0,1,3,4,\dots\}}(d)\le\exp(20n/d^{1/4})\,m(d)$, so excluding 2-dimensional subcubes reduces the count to essentially the number of perfect matchings.
